newsitem.title: CHINA: China '97 copper output seen exceeding 900,000 T.
newsitem.headline: China '97 copper output seen exceeding 900,000 T.

text.p: China's output of copper is expected to exceed 900,000 tonnes in 1997, up slightly from 1996, the Market Daily said on Tuesday.
China produced 909,700 tonnes of copper in 1996, up 5.71 percent from 1995, official figures showed.
Domestic demand for copper is expected to reach 1.05 million tonnes in 1997, up by about five percent from the 1996 level, the newspaper said.
China's copper imports were expected to remain at relatively high levels in 1997 because of projected weak international copper prices, it said, but gave no figures.
China's imports of uncast and raw copper rose 32.7 percent 714,248 tonnes in 1996, customs figures showed.
China's exports of uncast and raw copper reached 133,708 tonnes in 1996, up 2.5 percent from 1995, the figures showed.
